races.title: State Senate, District 26
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Sam Page
cands.bio: Rockingham County Sheriff since 1998, with over four decades in law enforcement as a patrolman, criminal investigator and administrator. U.S. Air Force security forces K-9 handler, 1975–1980. Sought the 2024 Republican nomination for lieutenant governor. Won the 2026 District 26 Senate race.
cands.gaps: We could not find his birthplace, where he was raised, or when he came to North Carolina. We found no record of any stance on data centers, development, growth or land conservation. We also found no stated position on homestead property taxes, limits on out-of-state or foreign land buyers, or H-1B visas and immigration enforcement from this research. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2024 or 2026. Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him. We found no news coverage or official findings about controversies. He has held no legislative office, so there is no legislative record. His campaign site describes his sheriff's office work only in general terms, with no specific actions we could verify.

qual.background: Elected Rockingham County Sheriff in 1998 and still serving as of 2024. Earlier worked as a patrolman, criminal investigator and administrator, and served in the U.S. Air Force from 1975 to 1980. He has not held legislative office.
qual.why: Nearly three decades in an elected local executive office and a long law-enforcement career fit the middle range. He has no prior legislative service and no listed policy or budget career, so he does not reach the high range.
qual.label: Nearly three decades in an elected local executive office and a long law-enforcement career fit the middle range. He has no prior legislative service and no listed policy or budget career, so he does not reach the high range.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: His campaign site says he will fight to raise teacher starting pay to $50,000, add incentives and pay increases for teachers, and allow "smart, accountable school choice with commonsense guardrails." It also says he wants policies to stop private schools from inflating tuition because of school choice vouchers.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site says he will work to strengthen penalties for violent offenders, push to restart the death penalty, and give law enforcement and prosecutors more tools to keep dangerous criminals off the streets.

cands.name: Steve Luking
cands.bio: Retired family physician from Reidsville, NC, born in Dayton, Ohio. Co-founded Reidsville Family Medicine and served as chief of staff and hospital board chair at Annie Penn Hospital. Democratic candidate for NC Senate District 26 in 2024 and 2026.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists 2026 voter guide recommendations from Sway voting groups, including Better Future NC, Fair Map Fight Club, Reject AIPAC from City Council to Congress, Unburdening The Ballot and Waves of Democracy. It found no endorsements for his 2024 run.

cands.gaps: The sources do not say where he was raised; his campaign site says only that his family roots span rural Georgia and rural Ohio. His campaign site's Issues page and the rest of his About page were not available, so his full platform is not covered. We found no statements from him on data centers, development, growth, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land purchases, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns or abortion. He has not held elected office, so there is no legislative record to review. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey.

local.label: Roots 55: He was born in Ohio and says he moved to North Carolina in 1989 as an adult to start a practice, which means about 37 years in the state, mostly in Reidsville.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Family physician for about 35 years in Roxboro and Reidsville; co-founded Reidsville Family Medicine with his brother, a practice that cared for over 5,000 patients; chief of staff at Annie Penn Hospital.
qual.why: He has real-world experience running a medical practice and a long professional career, which fits the middle range. No prior legislative or elected service, or law, policy or budget career, appears in the sources. Hospital board and chief-of-staff roles were not counted toward the score.
